name: Slider Lateral Lunge
summary: A unilateral lower-body exercise where one foot slides laterally while the opposite leg squats down, developing quad, glute, and adductor strength and mobility.

setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, placing one foot on a slider or gliding disc.
Keep the stationary foot firmly planted, carrying the vast majority of your body weight.
Clasp hands at your chest for balance, or hold a kettlebell or dumbbell in a goblet position.
steps: Hinge back at the hips and bend the knee of the stationary leg to descend into a squat.
Simultaneously slide the non-working leg straight out to the side, keeping the knee extended and toes pointing forward.
Lower yourself under control until the thigh of the working leg is roughly parallel to the floor.
Drive through the heel and midfoot of the stationary leg while actively pulling the sliding foot inward to return to the starting position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you sit back and slide the leg outward, and exhale as you drive up and pull the slider back to center.
cues: Sit back into the working hip.
Keep most of your weight on the planted foot.
Pull the floor together to stand.

common_faults.fault: Putting too much weight on the sliding foot, making it difficult to return and risking groin strain.
common_faults.correction: Keep roughly 80 to 90 percent of your body weight centered over the stationary leg throughout the entire repetition.

common_faults.fault: Working knee caving inward during the descent.
common_faults.correction: Actively track the knee of the squatting leg over the middle toes.
Keep the sliding leg fully straight to direct tension into the hips and stretch the adductors.

precautions: Use on a smooth, non-abrasive surface with adequate friction control.
Begin with bodyweight to test groin flexibility before introducing external loads.
